text:
Priya K.: quick PRD intake — we need a privacy-aware sampling + audit snapshotting feature for regulated customers. problem: customers want deterministic, reviewable samples of inference requests (for audits) but can’t send raw PII to us or keep full egress logs.
Maya R.: totally, core asks from finance/healthcare pilots. they want 0.1% sampled traces that are reconstructable for review but scrubbed by default.
Alex G.: tech constraints: we have streaming + prefix caching; adding sampling at the router level is feasible. question: where to hash/scrub? client-side vs server-side has tradeoffs.
Priya K.: goals: (1) per-tenant sampling policy, (2) deterministic sampling (stable hashes) so requested samples are reproducible, (3) automatic PII redaction & reversible audit-only envelopes for authorized reviewers, (4) low perf overhead (<1% latency p50). non-goals: full request storage for every tenant, realtime streaming of all samples to customers.
Chris L.: acceptance criteria idea: sample rate config in console, sampled record contains: model id, tokenized payload fingerprint, redaction map, reviewer-only audit blob (encrypted), and a hashed request id. UX must show sampled count + expected monthly cost.
Dan S.: customers also want opt-in manual sampling for particular request IDs (for debugging). need an API to mark specific request IDs for capture.
Alex G.: implementation sketch: router computes sample_hit = H(tenant_id || request_id) < threshold. store sampled blob to encrypted S3 + index in BigTable with encrypted pointer. provide a "reveal" endpoint that requires a signer from customer + our KMS to unwrap audit blob.
Priya K.: privacy pattern: default store scrubbed copy with stable fingerprint. audit blob = AES-GCM(encrypted_original) with access policy. legal: what retention window?
legal-bot: recommended default retention 90 days for encrypted audit blobs; longer retention needs a contract addendum. redact direct identifiers before storing scrubbed copy; reversible storage only for blobs with explicit customer consent.
Maya R.: edge cases: multi-tenant request (routing shared model) — must store tenant-scoped sample only; also cloud-to-private handoffs: private deployments should export a compatible sampling manifest.
Alex G.: perf numbers: rough calc — adding a hash + random compare on router adds ~0.6ms median; batch write to blob store async, impact negligible. need canary on 5% of routers.
Priya K.: success metrics: (A) customers can configure sampling policy in console & see sample counts within 24h, (B) 0 incidents of unauthorized reveal in 12 months, (C) <1% p50 latency regression for sampled tenants.
Chris L.: UI notes: sampling rule grammar: percentage, fixed-rate by tenant-id prefix, and manual request list. show simulated monthly storage & egress costs.
Dan S.: rollout plan: alpha with two pilot customers (one healthcare, one fintech) -> collect legal checklist -> beta @ 5 tenants -> GA. timeline ask: 6-8 weeks for alpha.
Priya K.: blockers: 1) legal sign-off on reversible storage, 2) KMS workflow for cross-tenant reveal, 3) console exposure for policy rules.
Alex G.: I'll spike router changes + reveal endpoint proto this week. Maya/Chris can start on acceptance test cases & console mocks.
Priya K.: thanks — can folks react with :thumbsup: if they’re aligned and drop followups below.
Maya R.: :thumbsup:
Chris L.: :thumbsup:
Alex G.: taking action — will post spike PR by EOD Friday.
Dan S.: added pilot customer contacts in the doc.
legal-bot: noted retention policy — will schedule a short review with legal ops on Thursday.
